claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr and MoNbTaW can serve as single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy-alloy systems for the proposed comparison.
The initial random-solid-solution state has negligible chemical short-range order.
Force-constant fluctuations and mass disorder in the random state strongly scatter phonons and lower lattice thermal conductivity.
An equilibrium SRO state can be generated for MoNbTaW at about 800 K.
Thermal annealing can make SRO clusters reach a percolating state in the proposed bcc alloys.
The SRO state is stable in a single-phase bcc structure at operating temperatures above 800 K.
Heat transport in the stated high-temperature regime is dominated by lattice vibrations rather than electronic contributions.
Percolating SRO clusters form a connected network of chemically ordered domains within the disordered matrix.
The connected SRO network reduces the effective force-constant variance along its percolation paths relative to the random state.
Standard scattering models predict that SRO increases disorder and reduces thermal conductivity.
Percolating SRO domains create a coherent, superlattice-like phonon-transport pathway with locally minimized or correlated force-constant fluctuations.
The coherent pathway reduces long-wavelength acoustic-phonon scattering and delays attainment of the Ioffe-Regel limit to higher energies.
Long-wavelength acoustic phonons dominate heat transport at high temperatures in the proposed alloys.
In fcc systems, SRO acts purely as an additional phonon-scattering center.
Once SRO percolates, lattice thermal conductivity will be higher than in the random state, or its suppression will be substantially smaller than predicted by mixing and scattering models.
The temperature dependence of lattice thermal conductivity will show a distinct transition associated with the SRO percolation threshold.
The proposed mechanism applies only when SRO domains are sufficiently chemically distinct to alter force constants, sufficiently coherent to connect, and above their percolation threshold.

A series of annealed specimens will be compared using APT/HRTEM for SRO connectivity, TDTR for lattice thermal conductivity, INS for phonon linewidths and lifetimes, and EXAFS or DFT for force-constant variance.

The proposed percolative-highway mechanism is falsified if conductivity decreases monotonically with SRO fraction through the established percolation point while phonon linewidths remain broad or broaden further.
The existence and critical volume fraction of an experimentally accessible SRO percolation transition in bcc RHEAs are presently unknown.
